docs.summary:
Which layers collide with which, as a symmetric 32x32 bit matrix.

Process-global rather than per [`PhysicsWorld`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.PhysicsWorld), so every scene shares one matrix. That is deliberate (the editor exposes it as a project setting), but it does mean two scenes cannot disagree.

docs.summary: Sets whether a layer collides with every layer, itself included.

Replaces the whole matrix from packed rows, one bit per pair. Loading it a pair at a time would copy the matrix once per bit, and would let a reader catch it half applied.

The result is forced symmetric: filtering asks about a pair in whatever order the broad phase produced it, so an asymmetric matrix would make collisions depend on that order.
The matrix as packed rows, one bit per pair.
Restores the engine default, where every layer collides with every other.
Which layers the given one collides with, indexed by layer.
Forces the matrix symmetric by taking the union of the two triangles. Every setter here is already symmetric, so this only matters after a matrix was assembled elsewhere.
Changes every time the matrix is written.
